discovery-weak-signals.name: grid and load-center infrastructure exposure

discovery-weak-signals.name: backlog growth with contract-quality caveat
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Large RPO/backlog growth supports demand visibility, while MSA/non-fixed-price components make headline backlog less firm than fully contracted obligations.

adversarial-red-team.name: concentration risk
adversarial-red-team.basis: current 10-Q reports no >=10% revenue or receivable customer

adversarial-red-team.name: execution risk
adversarial-red-team.basis: large projects and rapid scaling can create margin and working-capital volatility

expectations-execution.name: execution and earnings conversion
expectations-execution.basis: revenue growth translated into substantially higher GAAP and adjusted per-share earnings

expectations-execution.name: cash generation and liquidity
expectations-execution.basis: Strong operating cash generation and available liquidity support execution of a capital-intensive growth and acquisition program.

items.risk: Large-project execution, skilled-labor availability and customer capital-program timing can create delivery volatility.
Acquisition activity and project mix can make headline growth less comparable across periods.
Skilled-labor, permitting, customer capex timing and large-project execution can shift the bottleneck from demand to delivery capacity.
Backlog is not equivalent to risk-free future revenue; project timing, customer financing and execution can alter conversion.
Acquisitions and project mix can obscure organic comparability and margin durability.
Backlog includes estimated MSA orders/renewals and non-fixed-price contracts; many customer contracts can be terminated on short notice, limiting the certainty implied by headline backlog.
Capital intensity and acquisition spending are substantial: six-month acquisition cash use was $930.3M and capex was $451.0M, while commercial paper outstanding was $448M at June 30.
Backlog quality may be weaker than the headline total implies because MSA estimates and terminable contracts can fail to convert at assumed volumes or timing.
Sustained acquisition/capex intensity could pressure funding flexibility if operating cash conversion deteriorates.
Management explicitly flags weather, regulatory, permitting, supply-chain, inflation, interest-rate and recession risks to project timing and results; raised guidance remains forward-looking.
